Fundraising & Community Leadership Role | $500K Revenue Responsibility Across Raleigh, Charlotte & South Carolina

The Development Manager is responsible for fundraising results, volunteer leadership, and key chapter activities across a defined three‑community territory that includes Raleigh, Charlotte, and South Carolina. This role is accountable for achieving approximately $500K in planned annual fundraising revenue across the territory.​​


This position is the face of the Foundation within the territory and the first point of contact for chapter members, volunteers, donors, and local partners. They build strong, trusted relationships with individuals, businesses, and community organizations, connect people to local resources, and help share scientific advancements in ways that are meaningful and accessible.

This is a hands‑on fundraising and leadership role that blends clear goal accountability with strong collaboration. The Development Manager develops and implements fundraising strategies, partners closely with volunteer committees, and grows event and community‑based revenue—working in close coordination with internal teams and grounded in the Foundation’s collaborative, mission‑driven culture.

Key Responsibilities
Grounded in the Foundation’s collaborative, mission‑driven culture, this role blends clear fundraising accountability with relationship‑based, community‑centered work. The following are representative of the duties and responsibilities associated with this position and are not meant to be an all-inclusive list.
  • Plan and carry out fundraising strategies that grow revenue year over year across assigned communities.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with volunteers, donors, local businesses, sponsors, and community partners.
  • Work closely with volunteer committees to plan and execute successful fundraising events and activities.
  • Partner with the Regional Director and internal teams to set priorities, milestones, and measures of success for the territory.
  • Recruit, support, and motivate volunteer leaders, helping them feel connected, effective, and appreciated over time.
  • Serve as the Foundation’s primary representative in the community—sharing resources, building awareness, and communicating scientific progress in accessible, meaningful ways.
  • Use the donor database to track engagement, understand giving potential, support outreach, and inform fundraising decisions.
  • Tailor approaches to the unique strengths and needs of each community, offering guidance that helps chapters grow and succeed.
  • Manage community materials and resources needed to support events and local engagement.
  • Build enough scientific understanding to confidently explain the Foundation’s work and describe the impact it has on individuals and families.

Essential Qualifications Include:
  • Must have 3-5+ years of experience in fundraising, community engagement, development, volunteer management or a related non-profit role
  • Demonstrated success meeting or growing revenue goals, including individual giving, corporate sponsorships, peer‑to‑peer fundraising, or event‑based fundraising
  • Strong relationship‑builder with the ability to engage and sustain authentic connections with volunteers, donors, community partners, and local businesses
  • Experience recruiting, supporting, and working effectively with volunteer leaders, including committees or chapter‑based volunteers
  • Comfortable serving as a visible, public‑facing representative within local communities
  • Well organized, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, stakeholders, and events across a defined territory
  • Experience using a donor database or CRM (such as Salesforce, Raiser’s Edge, or similar) to track engagement, run reports, and support fundraising efforts
  • Clear and compassionate communicator, able to explain complex information in ways that are accessible and meaningful
  • Able to work independently while collaborating closely with internal teams in a remote environment
  • Willingness to learn and communicate scientific or technical information at a high level to support education and engagement
  • Comfortable with regular regional travel and occasional evening or weekend work for events
  • Proficient with everyday technology tools, including Microsoft 365, Zoom, databases, and calendars Experience working with chapter‑based or volunteer‑led networks is preferred

Position Specifics:
  • Internal title: Community Manager- MidSouth Territory
  • Territory Specifics: Established Chapters; Existing Volunteer Leadership
  • Location: Remote/ Home-Office (Based on Raleigh, Triangle, or Charlotte area with regional travel)
  • Compensation: Budgeted starting salary range: $80,000- 90,000/yr, commensurate with experience and aligned with geographic market considerations and internal equity. Additional 5% annual incentive bonus eligibilty.
  • Tools & support:Company-provided HP or Mac laptop, monitor, printer, and a $120 monthly technology stipend
  • Schedule: Full‑time, Monday–Friday, with flexibility; occasional evenings and weekends required for events
  • Reporting relationship: Reports to the Regional Director
  • People management: No direct reports

Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

Imagine joining a team where the first day begins with a challenge that matters. The Senior Lead Architect is trusted to think boldly, take ownership, and bring fresh ideas to problems that shape the future of AI-ready connectivity. In this high-accountability environment, innovation is not just encouraged—it is expected. Leaders provide clarity, teammates offer trust, and every contribution has a visible impact on customers, partners, and the industry.
As the Senior Lead Architect’s influence grows, so does the opportunity to lead. They help shape the organization’s strategic vision, connecting diverse ideas into architectural solutions that drive business outcomes. Colleagues across the company seek the Senior Lead Architect’s expertise to solve unique and complex challenges, recognizing their ability to see beyond immediate requirements and create scalable, future-focused designs.
Over time, the Senior Lead Architect becomes a catalyst for transformation, leading highly complex initiatives that span multiple disciplines and business units. Their work creates meaningful impact, advances innovation, and helps define what comes next. If you are motivated by challenging work, empowered by trust, and inspired by the opportunity to make a lasting difference, this is where your story can begin.

Location

This is a work from home position within the US.

The Main Responsibilities

  • Optical Strategist: translate emerging technologies into deployable architecture, standards, vendor requirements, and operational models
  • Architectural Recommendations: include technology roadmaps, reference architectures, lifecycle planning, and interoperability requirements.
  • Visionary: Envision future optical network over a 1–3-year horizon and turn them into reality
  • Original Mindset: Think, how can we do this?
  • AI-Enabled Innovation: Use AI tools to accelerate research, network analytics, documentation, automation, modeling, and decision support.
  • Standard Bodies Participation: Engage in standard bodies such as an MSA, IEEE, OIF, Open ROADM, etc., to drive Lumen’s initiatives
  • Data Mining and Trending Analytics: Utilize strong data mining skills to extract network data and present current and trending demands
  • Financial Model Derivation: Fluent in TCO, ROI, NPV, sensitivity analysis, marginal cost, long-run average cost, capital efficiency, and demand-based forecasting.
  • Business Case Development: Develop business cases to support architectural designs and decisions
  • Automation Vision: Create an automation vision for the Optical Product line

What We Look For in a Candidate

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical, optical, or Telecommunication engineering, or 5-7+ years of equivalent experience and training.
  • Master of Business Administration, or 5-7+ Years of equivalent experience in financial modeling
  • Fluent in DWDM, Coherent Optics, ROADM/Open Line Systems, Optical performance modeling, and network resiliency
  • Strong analytical approach to solving problems
  • Experience communicating technical solutions from C-Level to entry level employees
  • Has been the technical subject matter expert that has successfully led a new Product introduction into the production network
  • Strong data extraction and analytic skills using tools like SQL and Power BI

    Preferred Qualifications:
  • Knowledge in the following areas: Quantum Encryption, HCF/MCF, APIs

raw.description:
Rockstar is recruiting for a company that is transforming the $20B deathcare industry. This modern funeral home operator has become the largest independent in California, now operating in four states, with hundreds of 5-star reviews and an 80+ NPS. They are building a fundamentally better experience for families during one of life's hardest moments, moving fast with a disciplined, high-trust team.

Location: United States (Remote)
Employment Type: Full time
Department: Marketing

About the Company

Deathcare is a $20B market in everybody's blindspot. It touches every family, yet remains fragmented, widely distrusted, and offline — all while the world around it has transformed. The company believes families deserve a fundamentally better experience.

At the company, they are building the modern funeral home. In under two years, they have become California's largest independent, are now in four states, and have earned hundreds of 5-star reviews and an 80+ NPS along the way.

The candidate would join a team that has built and scaled real-world businesses. The company is now expanding nationally with urgency, discipline, and plenty of meaningful work still ahead.

The Role

This is a marketing role that shapes the product, not one that answers to it.

At-Need is the company's largest business: families who have just lost someone and need to arrange a cremation or a funeral, usually within a few days. The industry they run into was built for the seller, not for them: opaque pricing, dated storefronts, and a transactional playbook that treats a profound moment like an upsell.

The company is the opposite, and this role makes that difference clear everywhere a family meets them. The person in this role will shape the customer journey and the offering itself, so a family can understand quickly why they can trust the company to do right by them. It is a big reason the company's NPS is 80+.

The role owns the full marketing funnel for At-Need, working closely with Sales, who owns the consultation and the close:

  • Positioning, packaging, and the voice of the company's core product
  • The marketing behind launching new markets, products, and consumer segments
  • The demand funnel that brings families to the company

What the Candidate Will Work On Early

  • Launch the company in new markets and reach new communities, building a repeatable playbook as they go
  • Position and package a new offering, funerals among them, and take it from concept to launch with Sales and Growth
  • Sharpen how the company shows up with its hospice and referral partners

This is real ownership of the company's biggest business line. The candidate will shape the future of the company's products, not execute a roadmap someone handed them.

What the Company Is Looking For

The company cares far more about the quality of the candidate's work, and the kind of companies they have done it at, than their title. The strongest signal is having sold something similar, a high-trust and high-consideration service, to similar people, at a similar price.

  • Positioning and offering judgment: The candidate shapes what the offer is and how it is framed, not just describes what someone else built. They build the messaging everything else pulls from, and they can create and package a new offering from scratch.
  • Prioritization and rigor: The candidate turns an ambiguous goal into a sequenced plan, they can say out loud what they are not doing and why, and they reach for the numbers by instinct.
  • Consumer instinct: The candidate gets inside the head of someone making a hard, emotional decision in one of the worst weeks of their life, and turns that into messaging that resonates and converts. They know how trust is built and broken in a sensitive category.
  • Hands-on and high-agency: The candidate is in the ad account, the landing page, and the brief themselves. They move without being pushed and they close loops.

The candidate does not need to be a mathematician or a copywriter. They do need recent, personal ownership of the work, not a track record of directing others to do it.

Why Join

  • Do work that matters: help families through one of life's hardest moments with clarity and care
  • Own what matters: own the marketing for the company's biggest business line, with real scope and autonomy
  • A consumer story worth telling, in a category most people look away from, and one that has nothing to do with AI
  • Work with adults: high trust, low drama, smart people moving fast
  • A role that grows with its owner: broader marketing leadership is on the table for someone who earns it
  • Competitive salary, meaningful equity, and generous health, dental, and vision coverage

Compensation

$145K – $175K • Offers Equity

The company has taken a disciplined approach to compensation from day one. It's the only way to keep things consistent, fair, and strategic — so both the team and company can grow in a healthy way. They set ranges using benchmarking data (including Pave.com, the best source for early-stage companies since it pulls directly from HR systems).

Offers are based on three factors:

  • Performance potential: how the candidate performed in interviews and how closely their experience matches the role
  • Seniority: the depth of their relevant experience
  • Location: cost of living differences

raw.description:
Who We Are

Aspenware empowers mountain resorts and ski areas to deliver the ideal digital guest experience. Our guest-facing ecommerce and registration software is the most capable in the industry and is used by millions of skiers worldwide to process over a billion dollars in annual sales. The resorts we work with trust the innovation and thought leadership that Aspenware provides, and they leverage the operational advantages of our platform to grow their businesses.
We are a talented and high-performing team and welcome the opportunity to learn from one another.
Aspenware makes hiring decisions based on how well candidates align with our Core Values. Aspenware employees are…
Dependable: We take ownership. We are accountable and adaptable. We have a can-do attitude and are willing to pivot.
Caring: We care about our co-workers and our clients. We are mindful of and inspired by the impact our work has on our communities.
Innovative: We are thought leaders who bring creativity and a desire for innovation to everything we do. We are continually improving ourselves and our surroundings.
Curious: We challenge default processes while assuming best intent, seeking to understand before judging. We ask good questions to spark learning, better decisions, and smarter outcomes. We make the extra effort to gain a deeper understanding of a situation so we can provide better solutions.

What You Will Do

This role owns the upgrade and release process end-to-end, including customer and internal communications, status updates, deployment, release notes, smoke testing, and ensuring every customer upgrade is successful, tracked, planned, and on schedule. You'll serve as the link between Engineering, QA, Customer Success, and Product during every release cycle, giving leadership and customers clear visibility into where a release stands at all times. This is a hands-on role for someone who wants ownership over a process and can apply their platform knowledge to troubleshoot issues as they arise.

Your focus areas will include:

  • Release Coordination: Own the end-to-end release process for both planned and hotfix releases, keeping every stage on track from regression through production.
  • Track releases through regression, beta, and production in partnership with QA and Engineering; escalate risks, blockers, and scope changes as needed.
  • Create deployment checklists, perform CLTs, upgrade test environments, conduct test executions, and support client UAT; tag releases and coordinate production deployments with Engineering.
  • Publish release timelines and milestones; schedule and facilitate release-related meetings; communicate upgrade progress to customers and internal teams.
  • Draft, upload, and maintain release notes on the HUB; coordinate beta, pilot, and early-adopter selection with Customer Success and Product; maintain project plans, dashboards, and status reporting in Jira.
  • Customer Upgrade Communications: Lead customers through every step of the upgrade process, ensuring they understand what to expect, what is required of them, and where things stand. Proactively communicate status updates, next steps, timelines, and any changes so no customer is left waiting or guessing.
  • Customer Success Support: Support the Customer Success team with support tickets and tasks, drawing on Aspenware platform expertise to diagnose configuration issues and guide customers through the upgrade process.
  • QA Testing Support: Assist the Quality Assurance team with regression and QA testing when customer upgrades are not in progress, applying platform knowledge to identify and contextualize issues as they surface.

Who You Are

You're organized and calm under the pressure of a release week, and you default to over-communicating status rather than waiting to be asked. You're comfortable being the person who chases down an answer from Engineering, QA, Customer Success, Product, and a customer in the same afternoon. You bring solid project-coordination instincts (planning, tracking, reporting) and apply them in service of the release. Most importantly, you know the Aspenware platform well enough to recognize when something looks wrong and understand why, because the most critical moments in this role happen when things don't go as planned.

Required qualifications:

  • 2–3 years of hands-on experience with Aspenware Commerce, RTP, or comparable mountain resort ecommerce software
  • Experience working in or directly with the ski or outdoor resort industry
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills across technical and client-facing audiences
  • Proven ability to track and report status across multiple concurrent workstreams
  • Comfort working directly with Engineering/QA to own a process end-to-end, not just monitor it

Bonus points:

  • Prior experience as a Release Manager or Release Coordinator
  • Working knowledge of a software release lifecycle (regression, beta, production)
  • Experience with QA testing and Customer Service
  • Experience coordinating Agile software delivery using Jira
  • Familiarity with Git / release branching and tagging
  • Experience with JIRA Service Manager, Confluence, or X-Ray

What's In It for You

  • 4 weeks of PTO to start; increases with seniority
  • 11 paid holidays
  • 6 days of sick time
  • Paid parental leave for both primary and secondary parents
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Life insurance
  • 401k plan with a 5% match
  • Annual all-company ski day
  • National Park Pass
  • Annual Wellness Stipend
Salary: $65,000.00-$75,000.00

raw.description:
Meet the Moment with Alteryx

We're living through a once-in-a-generation shift in how work gets done. Data, automation, and AI are quickly becoming the center of every business decision - and Alteryx is leading the transformation.

You'll be working on the challenges that sit at the heart of modern business. No matter your role, the work you do will help organizations move faster, see more clearly, and tackle questions that used to feel impossible.

If you're ready to meet the moment with innovation, curiosity, and excellence, there's a place for you here.

Alteryx is searching for a Sr. Technical Program Manager (Security & Compliance). This position is remote-friendly.

Position Overview:

At Alteryx, we put data and AI to work for the intelligent enterprise. Alteryx One connects data, governed business logic, and AI-driven insights and actions in a scalable platform.

We are seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager to coordinate complex, cross-functional initiatives across Information Security, partnering heavily with Engineering, Legal, Product and IT.

This role will coordinate execution across the Information Security portfolio by maintaining integrated program plans and operating cadences, tracking dependencies and commitments, surfacing risks and decisions, and providing leaders with clear visibility into progress. The portfolio includes initiatives spanning identity and access management, vulnerability management, infrastructure and product security, data protection, compliance, incident readiness, and secure software delivery.

Success in this role requires strong technical fluency and disciplined execution. You will bring structure to ambiguous challenges, build alignment across organizational boundaries, and exercise sound judgment to strengthen trust, governance, and security throughout Alteryx’s products and systems.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Build and maintain integrated program plans, roadmaps, milestones, dependencies, decision points, ownership assignments, and success measures across the Information Security portfolio.

  • Coordinate complex initiatives spanning identity and access management, vulnerability management, infrastructure hardening, compliance and assurance, data protection, incident readiness, and secure software delivery.

  • Partner with accountable leaders across Information Security, IT, Infrastructure, Engineering, Product, Legal, and Privacy to maintain alignment and support effective execution.

  • Establish and manage operating cadences, including program reviews, working sessions, dependency reviews, decision tracking, and executive status reporting.

  • Track commitments, risks, issues, dependencies, and blockers; ensure they are assigned to the appropriate owner and escalated with clear context, impact, and decision requirements.

  • Translate business, technical, security, and regulatory objectives into coordinated execution plans without displacing the accountability of functional or program owners.

  • Facilitate cross-functional decisions and trade-off discussions across scope, schedule, quality, resources, security, and customer impact. Document outcomes and ensure follow-through.

  • Develop dashboards, metrics, and concise reporting that provide working teams and senior leaders with visibility into progress, risk movement, delivery confidence, and areas requiring intervention.

  • Strengthen organizational memory by maintaining reliable records of decisions, actions, dependencies, ownership, and program status.

  • Improve program execution through scalable processes, automation, AI-enabled workflows, and continuous improvement practices.

Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of relevant experience and a bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, engineering, information systems, cybersecurity, or a related field.

  • Proven success independently leading complex security, privacy, risk, compliance, or enterprise IT programs from strategy through delivery.

  • Expertise establishing program governance and operating mechanisms, including portfolio planning, OKRs, dependency and risk management, and executive reporting.

  • Excellent communication and influencing skills to drive alignment for technical teams, cross-functional partners, and senior leaders.

  • Strong analytical skills and experience using complex data and dashboards to guide prioritization, trade-offs, and program decisions.

  • Experience leveraging AI to improve engineering planning, execution, communication, and operational efficiency.

Valued Skills:

  • Enterprise SaaS, AI platform, analytics platform, or cloud infrastructure experience.

  • Experience applying automation or AI solutions to improve planning, execution, reporting, communication, or operational efficiency; relevant program management, security, cloud, or agile certifications are a plus.

  • PMP, SAFe, Scrum, AWS, Azure, or GCP certifications.

Compensation:

Alteryx is committed to fair, equitable, and transparent compensation. Final compensation will be determined by various factors such as your relevant work experience, education, certifications, skills, and geographic location.

The salary range for this role in the United States is $139,475 - $153,900.

In addition, you may be eligible for additional compensation, such as a bonus. Employees may also be eligible for a wide range of other benefits, including medical, retirement, financial, wellness, time off, employee discounts, and others.

Interested? Learn more and apply today at alteryx.com/careers!

Find yourself checking a lot of these boxes but doubting whether you should apply? At Alteryx, we support a growth mindset for our associates through all stages of their careers. If you meet some of the requirements and you share our values, we encourage you to apply. As part of our ongoing commitment to a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace, we’re invested in building teams with a wide variety of backgrounds, identities, and experiences.

CyberSecurity Operations Engineer (Graduate Considered)

A fantastic opportunity for a CyberSecurity Operations Engineer to join a fast-growing, technology-led security company delivering managed security and managed IT services to a global client base. This role sits firmly within the Operations and Service Delivery function, working closely with clients post-sale to support, implement and improve their security and IT environments.
This is a hands-on, client-facing operational role focused on technical support, troubleshooting, account ownership and project delivery.
Location: Fully remote, anywhere in the US
Salary: $80,000 – $120,000 per annum (lower end for a recent Graduate)
Requirements for CyberSecurity Operations Engineer:
  • Regardless of experience, you should have an outstanding academic background with a minimum GPA of 3.6
  • A Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cyber Security, Engineering, Mathematics or Physics
  • Degree obtained from a highly ranked academic institution (typically Top 100 US universities or equivalent globally)
  • Please ensure GPA and university are clearly listed on your CV
  • Hands-on technical experience through internships, commercial roles, homelabs, open-source projects or real-world environments
  • Strong technical understanding across operating systems, networking, security protocols, scripting and cloud infrastructure.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills with a practical, solutions-focused mindset
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to explain technical issues clearly to non-technical stakeholders
  • A proactive, self-motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced, high-responsibility environment
  • Curiosity, ambition and a genuine passion for technology and continuous learning
  • Exposure to SOC or offensive security is beneficial but not required - please note this it NOT a SOC analyst or penetration testing position, although you will gain exposure to both through collaboration with specialist internal teams.
Responsibilities for CyberSecurity Operations Engineer:
  • Deliver 1st and 2nd line technical support across security and IT environments
  • Take ownership of client issues from detection through to resolution
  • Act as a key technical point of contact for clients, managing ongoing relationships
  • Conduct regular client catch-ups and service reviews, discussing security and IT challenges
  • Guide clients through security and IT roadmaps, advising on best practice and improvements
  • Troubleshoot and support security software, agents and bespoke security controls
  • Triage and respond to security incidents raised by internal monitoring teams, advising on remediation
  • Design, implement and manage IT and cloud infrastructure across SaaS, PaaS and IaaS environments
  • Support device provisioning, hardening, monitoring and IT asset procurement
  • Assist with firewall management, compliance activities, reporting and documentation
  • Support pre-sales activity including demos and proof-of-concepts when required
  • Deliver and manage ad hoc security and IT projects involving multiple internal and external stakeholders
  • Support and mentor more junior team members as you progress within the team
What the role offers:
  • A highly varied operations role spanning security, IT support, projects and client delivery
  • Rapid technical development through real-world exposure to security and IT challenges
  • Clear progression into senior operations, account ownership or specialist technical roles
  • Structured training and support towards professional certifications
  • Opportunities to present internally and externally as your expertise develops
  • A collaborative, high-calibre team with strong technical standards
  • Fully remote working anywhere in the US
Applications:
If you would like to apply for this CyberSecurity Operations Engineer role, please submit an up-to-date CV via the relevant link. For your application to be progressed, academic results must be clearly listed, including GPA and university attended.

What You Will Do:

Energy Providers Partners lead at the intersection of industry transformation, client value, and practice growth. They build trusted executive relationships, anticipate market shifts, and bring the full breadth of the firm's expertise, technology, and delivery capabilities to help clients navigate three interconnected transformations: the transition to a cleaner, more resilient energy future; the modernization of utility operations and technology platforms; and the reinvention of business models, customer experiences, and ways of working.

Energy Providers Partners are not only trusted advisors to clients, but builders of the practice. They are responsible for shaping market strategy, developing talent, creating new growth opportunities, advancing the firm's thought leadership, and driving sustainable business outcomes for clients and Guidehouse alike. Through thought leadership, business development, talent cultivation, and delivery excellence, they create measurable value for clients while advancing the growth and market leadership of the Energy Providers practice.

The Key Account Partner serves as the executive owner of assigned accounts and is accountable for client satisfaction, revenue growth, profitability, forecasting accuracy, talent deployment, and the overall expansion of the firm's market presence within those accounts. This role requires a highly motivated and entrepreneurial leader with a proven track record of building executive relationships, driving growth, closing complex pursuits, and delivering measurable business outcomes for clients.

  • Lead the development, sale, and executive oversight of strategic advisory, technology modernization, business transformation, managed services, and risk management engagements for Investor-Owned Utilities and other energy sector clients.

  • Serve as the account leader of assigned accounts, responsible for developing and executing account strategies that deepen executive relationships, increase client value, and drive sustainable revenue, profitability, and market share growth.

  • Develop and expand C-suite and senior executive relationships that position Guidehouse as a trusted strategic partner and create opportunities for long-term account expansion and repeat business.

  • Help clients navigate Energy Transition, Technology Modernization, and Business Transformation by defining and executing strategies that improve performance, resilience, customer outcomes, and long-term enterprise value.

  • Identify emerging market trends, client priorities, regulatory developments, and industry disruptions, translating those insights into actionable growth strategies, differentiated solutions, and new business opportunities.

  • Shape, lead, and close complex pursuits, including opportunity origination, qualification, account planning, solution development, proposal strategy, executive presentations, negotiations, and contract execution.

  • Serve as the integrator of the firm's capabilities, proactively bringing together expertise, technology, managed services, and industry solutions from across Guidehouse to address clients' most strategic priorities and create differentiated value.

  • Provide executive sponsorship and governance for assigned accounts and engagements, ensuring delivery excellence, client satisfaction, quality, profitability, risk management, and achievement of intended business outcomes.

  • Drive portfolio and account performance through effective oversight of engagement quality, financial results, forecasting, pipeline health, risk management, resource strategy, and client relationship management. Accountable for achieving revenue, margin, bookings, and growth objectives across assigned clients and portfolios.

  • Lead annual and multi-year account planning efforts, maintaining accurate sales pipelines, revenue forecasts, investment plans, and growth strategies aligned with client priorities and firm objectives.

  • Expand client relationships by introducing innovative solutions, thought leadership, industry insights, and integrated Guidehouse capabilities that address evolving client needs and strengthen strategic partnerships.

  • Support the growth strategy of the Energy Providers practice by identifying emerging market opportunities, developing new offerings and solutions, and influencing go-to-market priorities and investment decisions.

  • Contribute to the firm's market presence through industry leadership, conference participation, executive engagement, publications, research, and the development of differentiated points of view that elevate Guidehouse's brand and market position.

  • Maintain deep expertise in the energy sector by monitoring industry developments, regulatory changes, emerging technologies, and market trends while cultivating relationships with key client and industry stakeholders.

  • Build, develop, and lead high-performing teams by attracting top talent, mentoring future leaders, creating career growth opportunities, and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and inclusion.

  • Lead and inspire teams to achieve ambitious growth, client impact, and delivery objectives while advancing the strategic priorities and long-term success of the Energy Providers practice.

  • Serve as a visible leader within Guidehouse, contributing to practice development, operational excellence, offering innovation, succession planning, and the continued growth and market leadership of the Energy Providers business.

What You Will Need:

  • 15+ years of experience leading client growth, account management, business development, and strategic consulting within the energy and utility sector, with strong market knowledge and relationships in the South U.S. utility market.

  • Deep understanding of the energy and utility industry, including utility operations, utility operational technology, grid modernization, customer and regulatory strategy, and emerging industry trends.

  • Demonstrated experience leading account strategy, financial planning, forecasting, and portfolio management, with accountability for revenue growth, profitability, pipeline development, and long-term client investment decisions.

  • Proven track record of originating, closing, and growing large, complex consulting, technology, and managed services engagements within Investor-Owned Utilities and other energy sector clients.

  • Demonstrated success serving as a trusted advisor to C-suite and senior executive stakeholders, building long-term relationships that drive measurable client outcomes and sustained business growth.

  • Experience developing and executing strategic account plans that drive revenue growth, profitability, market expansion, and client satisfaction.

  • Strong business acumen with the ability to identify client challenges, anticipate market shifts, and translate business needs into innovative, value-driven solutions.

  • Demonstrated ability to develop growth strategies, influence client investment decisions, and position differentiated solutions in highly competitive markets.

  • Proven ability to lead complex pursuits, including opportunity qualification, solution development, executive presentations, negotiations, and contract execution.

  • Exceptional strategic thinking, analytical, and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to connect industry trends, client priorities, and firm capabilities into actionable business strategies.

  • Outstanding executive communication and relationship-building skills, including the ability to influence decision-makers and communicate complex concepts to diverse audiences.

  • Experience leading large, cross-functional teams and managing multiple priorities while maintaining a focus on client outcomes, growth objectives, and operational excellence.

  • Demonstrated success developing, mentoring, and retaining high-performing teams while fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability, and innovation.

  • High degree of professional integrity, sound judgment, and commitment to ethical leadership.

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university.

  • Ability to travel as required to support clients, business development efforts, and team leadership responsibilities.

What Would Be Nice to Have:

  • MBA, Master's degree, or other relevant advanced degree in Business, Engineering, Public Policy, Economics, Energy, or a related field.

  • Demonstrated year over year experience of selling Multiple Million dollars of consulting and managed services annually

  • Prior Partner, Principal, Managing Director, Vice President, or equivalent leadership experience in a management consulting, professional services, or technology consulting environment.

  • Preference will be given to candidates with a commutable distance from Southeast Region.

The annual salary range for this position is $310,000.00-$520,000.00. Compensation decisions depend on a wide range of factors, including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, security clearances, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs.

What We Offer:

Guidehouse offers a comprehensive, total rewards package that includes competitive compensation and a flexible benefits package that reflects our commitment to creating a diverse and supportive workplace.

Benefits include:

  • Medical, Rx, Dental & Vision Insurance

  • Personal and Family Sick Time & Company Paid Holidays

  • Position may be eligible for a discretionary variable incentive bonus

  • Parental Leave and Adoption Assistance

Why this job is exciting

The role:

The Speech Analytics Analyst position partners with customers to uncover critical business drivers and needs. This position is responsible for leveraging and configuring the speech analytics platform to drive actionable solutions for customer care, sales, quality, compliance, operations, and marketing, and provides voice of the customer insight.

The Speech Analytics Analyst plays a critical role in the continuous improvement of the customer engagement model and shares a commitment to delivering products and services that make our customers thrive. You will help shape best in class AI solutions unparalleled in the Customer Experience landscape.

Responsibilities:

  • Using a curious and intuitive approach, determine what call events (keywords and phrases) to train the software to recognize as structured data to support analytics and business goals.
  • Analytical and knowledgeable, recognize pertinent language patterns and conversational content that lead to business value.
  • Review, calibrate, and validate the quality of data to verify analysis requirements.
  • Create stories from data analysis and communicate them to clients.
  • Create, edit, and manage custom dashboard reports.
  • Manage and maintain solution libraries that can be used across customers and industries.
  • Brainstorm value-added features and applications to use the available technology further.

Competencies:

  • Customer Focus: Builds strong customer relationships; Gains insight into customer needs; Identifies opportunities that benefit the customers; Builds and delivers solutions that meet customer expectations; Establishes and maintains effective customer relationships.
  • Analytical: Synthesizes complex or diverse information; Collects and researches data; Uses intuition and experience to complement data; Designs workflows and procedures.
  • Plans & Aligns: Sets objectives to align with broader organizational goals; breaks down objectives into appropriate initiatives and actions; stages activities with relevant milestones and schedules; anticipates and adjusts effective contingency plans.
  • Effective Communication: Delivers messages in a clear, compelling, and concise manner; Actively listens and checks for understanding; articulates messages in a way that is broadly understandable; Adjusts communication content and style to meet the needs of diverse stakeholders; Models and encourages the expression of diverse ideas and opinions.
  • Teamwork: Balances team and individual responsibilities; Exhibits objectivity and openness to others' views; Gives and welcomes feedback; Contributes to building a positive team spirit; Puts success of team above own interests; Able to build morale and group commitments to goals and objectives; Supports everyone's efforts to succeed.

Requirements:

  • Previous experience in a call/contact center or a firm grasp of conversational English.
  • Demonstrated strong analytical skills, adept at identifying patterns, and hypothesis-driven problem-solving.
  • Innovative mindset, aptitude for learning new technologies/software, and dexterity to adjust to changing priorities within an emerging business.
  • Self-starter who can act independently and work collaboratively.
  • Exceptional written and oral communication skills, including an ability to communicate across business areas.
  • Excellent listening & communication skills and a positive attitude are required for frequent interaction with customers.
  • Ability to work effectively with product development, engineers, and business team.
  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Communications, Statistics, or other quantitative-oriented fields or equivalent experience.

Preferred qualifications:

  • Knowledge of Contact Center business practices.
  • Quality Assurance / Agent Training experience.
  • Experience at startup based environment.

You are motivated by:

  • Hustle: You inspire others to work as hard as you. You will find a way, no matter how hard the task is.
  • Ownership: You have an owner/builder mentality. You care about what you deliver and own your mistakes.
  • Proactivity: You don’t wait for someone to tell you what to do or what problems to solve. You are always looking for ways to learn and improve.
  • Excellence: You set a high bar and surpass expectations. You hit your goals and ask for more.
  • Humility: You are not above any task in the organization and are willing to drop what you’re doing to help a teammate.

What you can expect from us

The team:

Capacity team members enjoy the opportunity and benefits of working at an artificial intelligence startup, but with leaders who’ve worked at places like Apple, Ebay, Visa, Answers.com, Oracle, Boeing, and many more world-class companies. The culture at Capacity encourages innovation, independent problem solving, and collaboration as we continue to mature our product in the ever-changing world of AI.

We provide:

  • Employer-paid health insurance (for you and your eligible dependents)
  • Profit Interest Units/incentive compensation
  • Unlimited vacation policy
  • 401(k) with a company match
  • Short term disability insurance
  • Group life AD&D insurance
  • A supportive, diverse workplace where we prioritize respect for each other and our clients
  • A fun and collaborative team culture

Salary range:

  • The expected base salary for the role is between $45,000 and $55,000; actual salary will be commensurate with a candidate's experience, skill and location.

Still unsure?

At Capacity we value more than just hard skills. Our goal is to build a holistic and diverse team. If you aren’t sure if you qualify, just apply! We will carefully consider your application and are always grateful for any time and effort invested in Capacity.

But wait, there’s more!

At Capacity we believe in more than just building amazing products and helping our customers. Although we are a remote workforce, we remember the neighborhood where we started. We still strive to elevate our community by furthering access to education and careers in the tech space. Our affiliated nonprofit, Create A Loop, brings rigorous computer science courses to underserved communities with little to no access to formal computer science education. There are many opportunities for our Capacity team members to serve and educate our Create A Loop students throughout the year.

About the Role

As a Senior Parametric Engineer, you’ll join a dedicated product team working closely with the Product Lead and technical specialists. The role is primarily focused on software development, covering geometry algorithms, optimisation, tooling, and cloud/backend engineering, with interaction with the product’s 3D interface.

You’ll have flexibility to shape the role based on your expertise and interests, while contributing to the product as it evolves.

Responsibilities

  • Develop geometry algorithms.
  • Work on computational optimisation.
  • Build internal tools.
  • Contribute to cloud and backend development.
  • Develop the standalone product, with around 99% of the role focused on C# development.
  • Write code that interacts with the product's 3D engine.
  • Collaborate directly with the product lead within the dedicated product team.
  • Collaborate with in-house Unreal specialists on interface work.
  • Work across a broad role scope that may evolve over time, with the balance of responsibilities shaped around your specific skills and interests and changing priorities.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of C# experience at an expert or advanced level. C# is the primary language for the product and there is no substitute for this requirement.

  • 3+ years of AEC computational design or geometry experience with a solid understanding. Computational or algorithmic design experience from adjacent domains such as manufacturing, robotics, CAD, simulation or games can be considered as a substitute.
  • 2–3 years of applied computational optimisation experience, or a strong applied mathematics/algorithms background with demonstrated optimisation experience.
  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience at mid-to-senior level is suggested, reflecting the depth needed for the core C# development work.

Nice to Have

  • 1–2 years of Unity, Unreal or 3D game engine experience with basic familiarity.
  • Understanding of 3D vector maths, mesh geometry, rendering and shaders, even without direct game engine experience.
  • Unity experience is useful in the short term and Unreal experience in the longer term as the product interface transitions from Unity to Unreal. In-house Unreal specialists lead this work directly, so engine expertise is a bonus rather than a requirement.

  • True Belonging: A long-term career where your contributions are valued

About Pinpoint

Pinpoint provides technology, training, certification, compliance, and sales-enablement solutions for organizations operating in complex and regulated industries. Our portfolio includes APEX MCS for Medicare certification and readiness, Inertia CS for compliance and risk workflows, and Vela LMS for enterprise learning, compliance training, and sales enablement.

Customers and prospects include Medicare carriers, FMOs, agencies, broker-dealers, financial-services firms, insurance organizations, compliance teams, training departments, and enterprise sales organizations.

The Opportunity

This is a hands-on role for a marketer who can move comfortably between strategy and execution. The Senior Growth Marketing Manager will shape positioning, build campaigns in HubSpot, create sales-enablement materials, support targeted outreach, and use funnel data to continuously improve results.

What You'll Own

  • Demand generation: Develop integrated campaigns for APEX MCS, Inertia CS, Vela LMS, and priority verticals using email, LinkedIn, landing pages, content, events, nurture, trials, and sales follow-up.
  • Audience and account targeting: Define ideal customer profiles, segment contacts and accounts, and create personalized or account-based outreach for priority buyers and industries.
  • Product marketing: Build positioning, personas, use cases, value propositions, proof points, comparisons, business cases, and launch messaging that turn complex capabilities into practical business value.
  • Sales enablement: Create presentations, one-pagers, ROI tools, infographics, case studies, email and LinkedIn messaging, objection-handling materials, and account-specific assets.
  • HubSpot and marketing operations: Build landing pages, forms, lists, workflows, nurture programs, lead routing, lifecycle processes, dashboards, and reporting; maintain reliable data flow with Salesforce.
  • Funnel optimization: Establish tracking and attribution standards, monitor conversion from engagement through pipeline, identify drop-offs, and test audiences, offers, messages, calls to action, and follow-up approaches.
  • Sales alignment: Partner with sales on priority accounts, campaign follow-up, lead-response expectations, recycling, re-engagement, and closed-loop feedback.
  • Events and customer growth: Run measurable pre-event, onsite, and post-event campaigns, and support customer adoption, renewal, cross-sell, upsell, testimonials, and case studies.

What Success Looks Like in the First Six Months

  • Clear positioning, target audiences, campaign priorities, and calls to action for APEX MCS, Inertia CS, and Vela LMS.
  • Improved product landing pages, forms, workflows, nurture programs, sequences, lead routing, and HubSpot/Salesforce reporting.
  • Targeted campaigns launched for priority Medicare, compliance, financial-services, insurance, and training audiences.
  • A reusable library of sales materials, including product summaries, comparisons, ROI tools, presentations, and outreach content.
  • Baseline funnel metrics established and measurable improvement in marketing-generated or marketing-influenced meetings, demonstrations, opportunities, and pipeline.
  • Stronger sales handoffs, event follow-up, and customer-expansion support.

Required Qualifications

  • Five or more years of B2B growth marketing, demand generation, product marketing, lifecycle marketing, or integrated marketing experience.
  • Demonstrated success generating qualified meetings, demonstrations, opportunities, or pipeline—not only awareness or engagement metrics.
  • Strong hands-on HubSpot experience across landing pages, forms, lists, workflows, email, automation, lead management, and reporting.
  • Strong business writing and product-marketing skills, with the ability to simplify technical, compliance, or operational concepts.
  • Ability to personally build and launch campaigns, collaborate closely with sales, manage multiple priorities, and use data to improve performance.

Preferred Experience

  • B2B SaaS, RegTech, InsurTech, FinTech, learning management, compliance, enterprise training, insurance, Medicare, or financial services.
  • Account-based marketing, mid-market or enterprise campaigns, conferences, product launches, trials, pilot programs, customer marketing, or cross-selling.
  • Responsible use of AI-enabled tools for research, personalization, content development, campaign execution, and analysis.

The Person We Are Looking For

Commercially minded, highly accountable, curious, organized, and resourceful. The successful candidate can simplify complicated information, communicate credibly with executives and sales teams, and is equally comfortable setting strategy, building a campaign, and presenting the results.

Job Description Summary

‎

The Manager, Cloud Architecture translates the enterprise cloud and infrastructure strategy into disciplined, day-to-day execution. Reporting to the Director of Cloud & Infrastructure Solutions, this role leads a team of systems engineers, network engineers, identity engineers, and access management specialists responsible for the reliability, security, and continuous optimization of Mosaic Health’s cloud and on-premises environments.
This is a player-coach position: technically credible enough to challenge design decisions and validate architectural proposals, and operationally strong enough to hold the team accountable to delivery standards, SLAs, and cost targets. The Manager is the Director’s primary execution partner and acts as the team’s single point of accountability for platform health, security posture, and operational quality.

‎

How will you make an impact & Requirements

‎

Responsibilities

Cloud Platform Execution

  • Execute the enterprise cloud strategy (Azure-primary, multi-cloud aware) across IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, and hybrid environments, ensuring the team delivers to architectural standards set by the Director.
  • Own day-to-day Azure operations — compute, storage, networking, identity, and cost governance — with full accountability for platform health and SLA adherence.
  • Lead FinOps execution: monitor cloud spend, enforce tagging and cost allocation standards, identify and deliver optimization targets, and report performance to the Director.
  • Oversee the SaaS portfolio operationally — ensuring integrations are secure, platforms are governed to standard, and lifecycle management is current.
  • Drive automation adoption across the team to eliminate manual toil, accelerate delivery, and improve operational consistency.

Infrastructure & Systems Engineering

  • Manage server, storage, and virtualization environments — compute lifecycle, hypervisor platforms, SAN/NAS/object storage — ensuring capacity, performance, and resilience standards are met.
  • Oversee endpoint and profile engineering, including Okta administration and access management, ensuring identity hygiene and least-privilege standards are maintained.
  • Lead the team’s contribution to high availability and disaster recovery capabilities — executing DR tests, maintaining runbooks, and ensuring audit-ready HIPAA contingency plan documentation.
  • Partner with network engineering peers to ensure cloud and infrastructure architecture integrates seamlessly with WAN/LAN and Zero Trust initiatives.

Identity & Access Management

  • Oversee IAM engineering operations — provisioning, deprovisioning, role-based access control, and privileged access management — ensuring controls satisfy HIPAA, HITRUST, and internal governance standards.
  • Govern Okta platform operations: SSO, MFA, lifecycle management, and integration with enterprise applications.
  • Work closely with InfoSec to ensure identity and access controls are current, auditable, and aligned with the organization’s Zero Trust architecture direction.

Team Leadership & Operational Excellence

  • Lead, develop, and retain a high-performing team of six to seven engineers across systems, network, and identity disciplines — setting clear expectations, coaching to growth, and managing performance proactively.
  • Establish and maintain operational cadences: incident management, change control, problem management, and capacity planning — all grounded in ITSM best practices.
  • Maintain enterprise monitoring and observability standards across infrastructure domains, ensuring the team operates proactively with full visibility into platform health.
  • Support vendor and partner management at the operational level — holding providers accountable to SLAs and escalating contract or performance issues to the Director.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional IT teams and business stakeholders as a trusted execution partner, communicating platform status, risk, and roadmap clearly and without jargon.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Network Administration, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure, systems engineering, or network engineering — with at least 2 years in a team lead or manager role.
  • Hands-on Azure expertise — compute, storage, networking, identity, cost management — with the depth to evaluate architectural proposals, identify risk, and hold engineers accountable to design standards.
  • Demonstrated experience managing identity and access environments, including Okta (SSO, MFA, lifecycle management) and enterprise IAM/PAM programs.
  • Experience with server and virtualization platforms (VMware/Hyper-V), SAN/NAS storage, and data center operations.
  • Working knowledge of network engineering principles — sufficient to coordinate with network engineers on cloud connectivity, segmentation, and Zero Trust integration.
  • Proven ability to lead DR/BC execution — test programs, runbook management, RTO/RPO validation — in a HIPAA-regulated environment.
  • Practical FinOps experience: cloud cost monitoring, tagging enforcement, rightsizing, and spend accountability reporting.
  • Direct experience operating in a HIPAA-regulated healthcare environment; working familiarity with HITRUST CSF and the infrastructure controls required to satisfy audit requirements.
  • Strong people leadership skills — coaching, performance management, and building team accountability culture.
  • Effective communicator: translates technical complexity into clear, outcome-oriented language for stakeholders and leadership.

Preferred

  • Microsoft Azure Administrator (AZ-104) or Azure Solutions Architect (AZ-305) certification.
  • Okta Certified Administrator or Okta Certified Consultant.
  • Experience with enterprise monitoring platforms (Azure Monitor, Sentinel, Defender for Cloud, or equivalent).
  • Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code and automation tooling (Terraform, Bicep, PowerShell, Ansible).
  • Experience in multi-entity or post-M&A environments with tenant consolidation or rationalization exposure.
  • ITIL Foundation or equivalent ITSM training.

Working closely with the Country GSSO Head, you will help cultivate a strong clinical research environment that supports global R&D priorities. Additionally, you will drive strategic alignment and continuous improvement by standardizing processes across LSOM Senior Managers, promoting best practices, encouraging digital innovation, and facilitating the systematic sharing of knowledge and lessons learned across teams.

  • Ensure the accountable delivery of the study portfolio assigned to LSOM Senior Managers.
  • Oversee and guide the country study portfolio through effective leadership of LSOM Senior Managers, aligning execution with global strategies and local priorities.
  • Provide strategic direction and support to LSOM Senior Managers in portfolio monitoring, driving local action plans, and resolving issues.
  • Serve as the primary escalation point for complex or systemic local study challenges, facilitating resolution and ensuring portfolio targets are met with quality and efficiency.
  • Lead the development and mentorship of LSOM Senior Managers to equip them for effective team leadership and operational excellence.
  • Build and maintain a high-performing leadership team that promotes accountability, collaboration, and resilience across the LSOM organization.
  • Facilitate close collaboration between global study strategy teams and local study teams to effectively manage the assigned portfolio.
  • Oversee coordination among country functional teams to ensure successful delivery of the country portfolio.
  • Support discussions on country study placements, considering country strengths and growth potential.
  • Act as a key advisor for site selection, identifying priority sites and allocating resources accordingly.
  • Support country-level risk assessments by proactively identifying and managing risks to delivery.
  • Ensure inspection readiness and provide hands-on support during inspections, including responsibility for storyboards.
  • Promote continuous operational improvements and encourage sharing of best practices.
  • Manage resource allocation and workload distribution among LSOM Senior Managers and the broader LSOM team, including both FSP and FTE, to optimize trial execution and align with global priorities.
  • Ensure compliance with relevant regulatory and quality standards.
  • Collaborate with the country head to engage cross-functional stakeholders, align on trial deliverables, and manage escalations as needed.

What we expect of you

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The candidate we seek is an individual with the following qualifications.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Doctorate degree and 3 years of clinical execution experience OR
  • Master’s degree and 7 years of clinical execution experience OR
  • Bachelor’s degree and 9 years of clinical execution experience OR
  • Associate’s degree and 12 years of clinical execution experience OR
  • High school diploma / GED and 14 years of clinical execution experience
  • In addition to meeting at least one of the above requirements, you must have a minimum of 3 years of experience directly managing people and/or leadership experience leading teams, projects, programs, or directing the allocation of resources. Your managerial experience may run concurrently with the required technical experience referenced above

Preferred Qualifications:

  • +8 years work experience in life sciences or medically related field, including 6 years of biopharmaceutical clinical research experience (clinical research experience obtained working on clinical trials at a biotech, pharmaceutical or CRO company)
  • Experience managing multiple teams / direct reports
  • Experience at or oversight of outside clinical research vendors (CRO’s, central labs, imaging vendors, etc.)
  • Experience working on global clinical trials, with highly effective communications skills and track record for improving site engagement, improving relationships with investigators, and operational efficiency

What you can expect of us

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

raw.description:
Overview

POSITION SUMMARY: The Director – Financial Reporting & Technical Accounting is a highly visible role within USAP’s corporate finance organization and is responsible for leading key aspects of the Company’s financial reporting, technical accounting, consolidation, and reporting infrastructure. This role oversees the preparation of accurate, timely, and well-supported financial reporting, including monthly consolidating financial statements, intercompany eliminations, U.S. GAAP financial statements, footnote disclosures, and annual audit support. This individual will serve as a technical accounting and reporting leader, supporting complex accounting areas such as revenue recognition, business combinations, purchase accounting, goodwill and intangible asset impairment, equity-based compensation, leases, and other significant accounting matters. The Director – Financial Reporting & Technical Accounting will also support the continued development of accounting policies, internal control documentation, reporting processes, and financial statement support designed to be scalable, audit-ready, and aligned with best-in-class public-company reporting expectations. As USAP continues to mature its reporting environment, this role will partner closely with the CAO, CFO, FP&A, tax, legal, revenue cycle management, platform CFOs, shared services, platform accounting, external auditors, and other business leaders to strengthen reporting quality, disclosure readiness, close discipline, SOX-readiness efforts, and cross-functional governance over financial reporting. A successful candidate will bring strong U.S. GAAP knowledge, analytical capability, leadership presence, and the ability to drive process improvement in a complex, multi-entity healthcare environment.

The base pay estimate for this role is $107,700-$183,100 annually. The final offer will depend on the skills, experience, and qualifications of the selected candidate. This range is for base pay only and does not include bonuses or other compensation. This position is eligible for an annual bonus. Bonuses are not guaranteed and are awarded based on company and individual performance.

Job Highlights

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: (The ideal candidate must be able to complete all physical requirements of the job with or without a reasonable accommodation)

  • Serves as a leader within the corporate accounting organization, supporting the development of a public-company-ready financial reporting function, including SEC-style reporting readiness, technical accounting governance, internal control maturity, reporting technology, and audit committee support.
  • Oversees the monthly financial reporting function and works closely with FP&A, revenue cycle management, platform CFOs, shared services and platform accounting teams, the tax department, and all other divisions of USAP as needed.
  • Leads continuous improvement of the monthly and quarterly close and reporting process, including accelerated close timelines, reporting calendar discipline, review controls, account analysis standards, variance review, financial statement tie-outs, and timely escalation of reporting issues.
  • Supports public-company-ready reporting processes, including financial statement preparation and review, footnote disclosures, MD&A and non-GAAP measure support, disclosure documentation, financial statement tie-outs, review controls, and reporting calendar discipline.
  • Supports SOX-readiness efforts, including process documentation, control design, control execution evidence, remediation tracking, and coordination with process owners.
  • Performs technical accounting research and prepares accounting analyses and whitepapers for complex U.S. GAAP matters, including revenue recognition, business combinations, purchase accounting, goodwill and intangible asset impairment, equity-based compensation, leases, debt and equity transactions, segment reporting, EPS considerations, related-party matters, and new accounting standard adoption.
  • Partners with the CAO, legal, FP&A, tax, treasury, internal audit, external advisors, and other stakeholders to support disclosure governance, cross-functional review of external reporting materials, reporting consistency, and audit-ready documentation.
  • Ensures timely and accurate financial reports in order to assist the CFO, CAO, the board and other senior executives in performing their responsibilities.
  • Provides accounting support to the business development team and other strategic initiatives, including evaluation of proposed transactions, acquisition-related accounting considerations, and related financial reporting impacts.
  • Partners with accounting, FP&A, Workday systems, and other finance leaders to improve reporting automation, data integrity, dashboarding, financial reporting analytics, and scalable reporting processes.
  • Participates in the development and maintenance of accounting policies, reporting procedures, and internal control documentation to support consistent application of U.S. GAAP and audit-ready reporting.
  • Serves as a key liaison with external auditors, managing audit requests, PBC deliverables, issue resolution, reporting timelines, audit-ready support for significant accounting and disclosure matters, and recurring audit status meetings during quarterly and annual reporting cycles.
  • Acts as an advisor from the financial perspective on any contracts (including leases) into which the company may enter.
  • Evaluates the financial reporting division structure and team plan for continual improvement of the efficiency and effectiveness of the group as well as provides individuals with professional and personal growth with emphasis on opportunities of individuals.
  • Supervises and mentors staff to develop their accounting and problem-solving skills.
  • Manages or participates in special projects as needed.
  • Performs other duties as assigned/requested.

Qualifications

KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES (KSAs):

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting and 7-10 years of progressing accounting, financial reporting, technical accounting, or audit experience required.
  • Public-company reporting, IPO readiness, or transaction-readiness experience strongly preferred, including preparation or review of SEC-style filings, MD&A, earnings release materials, disclosure controls, governance routines, and public-company-quality financial statements.
  • CPA required or strongly preferred; Big 4 or national public accounting experience preferred.
  • Experience with Workiva or similar external reporting platforms strongly preferred, including financial statement tie-out, disclosure management, version control, SEC filing support, and XBRL coordination.
  • Ability to prepare executive-level and audit committee materials, including summaries of technical accounting matters, reporting risks, audit status, internal control themes, and key financial reporting judgments.
  • Exposure to the healthcare industry preferred.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite required; experience with Workday Financials, consolidation/reporting tools, and reporting automation preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of U.S. GAAP, financial statement preparation, consolidations, technical accounting, and financial reporting controls.
  • Demonstrated ability to prepare, review, and support complex financial statements and footnote disclosures.
  • Ability to operate in a complex, multi-entity environment with significant intercompany activity and consolidation requirements.
  • Strong attention to detail, organizational discipline, and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced reporting environment.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex accounting, financial reporting, and U.S. GAAP matters to executive leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Energetic, forward-thinking, and creative with high ethical standards and an appropriate professional image.
  • Sound judgment, strong analytical capability, and ability to balance technical accounting requirements with practical business considerations.
  • Self-directed and collaborative leader with the ability to build trust and influence across finance, operations, legal, tax, and external advisor teams.
  • A good educator who is trustworthy and willing to share information and serve as a mentor.
  • A decisive individual who possesses a "big picture" perspective and is well versed in accounting and finance.
  • Demonstrated ability to work cooperatively with stakeholders, all staff members and external financial partners, banks, and other lenders.
  • Self-motivated; ability to work without direct supervision.
  • Ability to build effective working relationships across diverse teams and leadership styles.
  • Ability to read, write, and speak English.

*The physical demands described here are representative of those that may need to be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Occasional Standing
  • Occasional Walking
  • Frequent Sitting
  • Frequent hand, finger movement
  • Use office equipment (in office or remote)
  • Communicate verbally and in writing

This is a remote position.

The opportunity

Our client is seeking aSenior Software Engineerwith a passion for building high-quality software applications that improve the way people access healthcare.

You will join a highly collaborative engineering organization working alongside Software Engineers, Quality Engineers, Product Managers, Designers, and other stakeholders within an Agile/Scrum environment.

You will contribute to and enhance an activetelemedicine platform serving patients across all 50 U.S. states. The platform includes aPatient Dashboard, which enables patients to interact with their care team, and aClinician Dashboard, which enables healthcare professionals to view, manage, and communicate with patients.

This is a hands-on engineering role with significant ownership across the software development lifecycle, from technical design and implementation through testing, deployment, and production support.

About the client

Our client is a healthcare technology company focused on improving access to healthcare through digital and telemedicine solutions.

Its platform connects patients with healthcare professionals through intuitive digital experiences and provides the tools care teams need to manage and communicate with patients effectively.

The engineering team works in a collaborative Agile/Scrum environment, with a strong focus on software quality, maintainability, accessibility, repeatable engineering practices, and continuous improvement.

What you will do

General

  • Participate actively in the Agile/Scrum process, currently organized around two-week sprints.

  • Work with internal and external platform stakeholders to understand business requirements and translate them into actionable development tasks.

  • Communicate complex engineering concepts, technical decisions, and potential impacts to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Participate in task estimation, technical design, development, code reviews, testing, debugging, and defect resolution.

Technical
